question: Pulling of the earth gravitationally in the same direction by the sun and the moon causes:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Spring tides**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Spring Tides**

 
 
• Pulling of the **earth gravitationally in the same direction by the sun and the moon **causes **spring tides**.
 
• When** lunar and solar tides align**, they reinforce one another and create a larger overall tidal.
 
• The** high tides in this instance are higher than usual, and the low tides are lower** than usual.
 
• Regardless of the season, spring tides happen** twice each lunar month**.
 
• Spring tides take place at the **new and full moons**.
 
• During the moon's quarter phases, the **bulges cancel each other out since the sun and moon are at a right angle to one another**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High Tides**

 
 
• When the tide is high, it has** reached its highest point **and much of the shore is covered in water.
 
• This occurs as a body of **water approaches one of the two bulges produced by the moon's gravitational pull**.
 
 
 
• **Low Tides**
 
 
• At low tide, the **water recedes to its lowest point **and begins to move away from the beach.
 
• **Two bulges are created on Earth (and its oceans) **as a result of the moon's gravitational pull or tidal force: one at the location that is closest to the moon and the other on the side of the planet that is directly opposite the moon.
 
 
 
• **Neap Tides**
 
 
• **Seven days after a spring tide**, there is a period of** moderate tides known as a neap tide, which occurs when the sun and moon are at right angles to one another**.
 
• These tides also happen** twice a month**, just as spring tides.
 
• **Low tides are a little higher and high tides are a little lower** than usual during neap tide.
 
• When the moon is** "half full," in the first and third quarters**, neap tides occur.
